text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Editorial says the pro-government press has attacked a ruling party MP and its founder Azem Hajdari of links with the former secret police Sigurimi.
- Companies and individuals donate money to journalist Arban Hasani fined $2,160 for slander. If fine was not paid by November 25, Hasani would be jailed for seven months.
- Construction companies repairing a wrecked flat of the appeals court chairman Prel Martini stopped work to complain they were not being paid enough.
- Some small trade unions accuse leader of the Independent Trade Union Valer Xheka of corruption.
- World Bank and IMF have sent delegations to Albania to press its government on the future of pyramid schemes.
- A World Bank delegation meeting all state-owned banks in Albania to discuss their privatisation.
- Opposition politicians saying privatisation of strategic sectors of the country is debatable because of the way the process is conducted by the governing Democratic Party.
- Police arrested 21 people charged of many crimes and organising a gangsters' band in the southern town of Berat.
- French city of Arles gives Jusuf Vrioni, a well-known Albanian literature translator, a "honorary citizen" title.

- A leader of the opposition Socialist Party says Tirana branch members said the party head, jailed Fatos Nano, and two other leaders were the cause of the loss in the local elections and they should leave the party.
- In an interview with the Italian newspaper La Gazzetta del Mezzogiorno, President Berisha promises Albania will closely cooperate with Italy to halt the smuggling of Albanian immigrants.
- President Berisha congratulates Romania's president-elect Emil Constantinescu on his victory in presidential elections.

- Reuters News Agency says Albanian arms have been found in death zones in Rwanda and Eastern Zaire. "Documents found by British reporters near the abandoned Hutu refugee camp in Goma, eastern Zaire, appeared to show that the company helped to arrange shipments of mortars, rifles and heavy machinegun ammunition from third countries including Israel and Albania."
